17"""Triton implementation of ``torch.linalg.eigvalsh`` for small batched matrices. 

18 

19One Triton program owns one full ``n x n`` symmetric operator held as a 

20pow2-padded, register-resident 2D tile. The operator is reconstructed from the 

21triangle selected by ``UPLO`` and diagonalised with threshold Jacobi sweeps: 

22plane rotations are applied in-register and a rotation is skipped outright when 

23its off-diagonal element is already below the working-precision floor. The 

24resulting diagonal is sorted ascending with a rank-based comparison sort. 

25 

26The exact matrix order ``n`` is a ``tl.constexpr`` so the sweep enumerates only 

27the ``n(n-1)/2`` real index pairs rather than the pow2-padded ``N(N-1)/2``. 

28 

29All computation that produces the returned values happens inside the device 

30kernel; the host wrapper only allocates the output, reads metadata and launches. 

31""" 

32 

33import logging 

34 

35import torch 

36import triton 

37import triton.language as tl 

38 

39logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) 

40 

41 

42# Maximum number of threshold-Jacobi sweeps. Cyclic Jacobi converges 

43# quadratically, so a small bound reaches machine precision for the small ``n`` 

44# this kernel targets (n <= 16). 

45_SWEEPS = 8 

46 

47 

48@triton.jit 

49def _eigvalsh_jacobi_kernel( 

50 A_ptr, 

51 Out_ptr, 

52 s_b, 

53 s_r, 

54 s_c, 

55 s_o, 

56 NP: tl.constexpr, 

57 N: tl.constexpr, 

58 SWEEPS: tl.constexpr, 

59 UPLO_L: tl.constexpr, 

60 THRESH: tl.constexpr, 

61): 

62 pid = tl.program_id(0) 

63 ri = tl.arange(0, N) 

64 ci = tl.arange(0, N) 

65 

66 # ---------------------------------------------------------------- load 

67 mask = (ri[:, None] < NP) & (ci[None, :] < NP) 

68 ptr = A_ptr + pid * s_b + ri[:, None] * s_r + ci[None, :] * s_c 

69 t = tl.load(ptr, mask=mask, other=0.0) 

70 

71 # Rebuild the full symmetric operator from the selected triangle. 

72 tt = tl.trans(t) # tt[i, j] = t[j, i] 

73 if UPLO_L: 

74 A = tl.where(ri[:, None] >= ci[None, :], t, tt) 

75 else: 

76 A = tl.where(ri[:, None] <= ci[None, :], t, tt) 

77 

78 # ------------------------------------------------------- Jacobi sweeps 

79 # Threshold Jacobi: a rotation whose off-diagonal element is already below 

80 # the working-precision floor cannot move the eigenvalues (perturbation is 

81 # O(|a_pq|)), so it is skipped entirely. The per-pair test costs one masked 

82 # tile reduction; the skipped rotation would have cost five tile broadcasts, 

83 # the two row extractions and the rotation block. The largest |a_pq| seen 

84 # during a sweep is accumulated for free from the values that test already 

85 # produced; once a whole sweep stays at or below the threshold the matrix is 

86 # converged and every remaining sweep is skipped outright. 

87 thresh = tl.max(tl.abs(A)) * THRESH 

88 maxoff = 2.0 * thresh 

89 for _ in range(SWEEPS): 

90 if maxoff > thresh: 

91 mx = thresh * 0.0 

92 for p in tl.static_range(0, NP - 1): 

93 for q in tl.static_range(p + 1, NP): 

94 apq = tl.sum( 

95 tl.where((ri[:, None] == p) & (ci[None, :] == q), A, 0.0) 

96 ) 

97 mx = tl.maximum(mx, tl.abs(apq)) 

98 if tl.abs(apq) > thresh: 

99 rowp = tl.sum(tl.where(ri[:, None] == p, A, 0.0), axis=0) 

100 rowq = tl.sum(tl.where(ri[:, None] == q, A, 0.0), axis=0) 

101 

102 app = tl.sum(tl.where(ri == p, rowp, 0.0)) 

103 aqq = tl.sum(tl.where(ri == q, rowq, 0.0)) 

104 

105 # Rotation cosine/sine of the annihilating angle, in a 

106 # form that needs only one square root and one 

107 # reciprocal square root: with d1 = aqq-app, 

108 # rr = sqrt(d1^2+4*apq^2) and qv = |d1| + rr the exact 

109 # rotation is 

110 # cos = qv * rsqrt(2*rr*qv) 

111 # sin = sign(d1)*2*apq * rsqrt(2*rr*qv) 

112 # which satisfies cos^2 + sin^2 = 1 by construction. 

113 d1 = aqq - app 

114 rr = tl.sqrt(d1 * d1 + 4.0 * apq * apq) 

115 qv = tl.abs(d1) + rr 

116 iw = tl.rsqrt(2.0 * rr * qv) 

117 c = qv * iw 

118 s = tl.where(d1 >= 0.0, 2.0 * apq * iw, -2.0 * apq * iw) 

119 

120 # Exact rotated diagonal entries, from c and s directly. 

121 c2 = c * c 

122 s2 = s * s 

123 cs = 2.0 * c * s 

124 dpp = c2 * app - cs * apq + s2 * aqq 

125 dqq = s2 * app + cs * apq + c2 * aqq 

126 

127 # New rows of A' = J^T A J. The generic expression 

128 # c*rowp - s*rowq is exact for every column outside 

129 # {p,q}; the rotated 2x2 block is patched in place so 

130 # that the same two vectors, broadcast along rows and 

131 # along columns, already carry the exact (p,p)/(q,q) 

132 # diagonals and the exactly zero (p,q)/(q,p) corners. 

133 nrowp = tl.where( 

134 ri == p, 

135 dpp, 

136 tl.where(ri == q, 0.0, c * rowp - s * rowq), 

137 ) 

138 nrowq = tl.where( 

139 ri == q, 

140 dqq, 

141 tl.where(ri == p, 0.0, s * rowp + c * rowq), 

142 ) 

143 

144 A = tl.where(ri[:, None] == p, nrowp[None, :], A) 

145 A = tl.where(ri[:, None] == q, nrowq[None, :], A) 

146 A = tl.where(ci[None, :] == p, nrowp[:, None], A) 

147 A = tl.where(ci[None, :] == q, nrowq[:, None], A) 

148 maxoff = mx 

149 

150 # ------------------------------------------------------ sort ascending 

151 diag = tl.sum(tl.where(ri[:, None] == ci[None, :], A, 0.0), axis=1) 

152 # Padded lanes must sort to the tail. 

153 diag = tl.where(ri < NP, diag, float("inf")) 

154 

155 lt = (diag[:, None] > diag[None, :]) | ( 

156 (diag[:, None] == diag[None, :]) & (ri[:, None] > ri[None, :]) 

157 ) 

158 rank = tl.sum(lt.to(tl.int32), axis=1) 

159 

160 vals = tl.sum(tl.where(rank[:, None] == ri[None, :], diag[:, None], 0.0), axis=0) 

161 tl.store(Out_ptr + pid * s_o + ri, vals, mask=ri < NP) 

162 

163 

164def linalg_eigvalsh(self, UPLO="L"): 

165 # ``aten::linalg_eigvalsh(Tensor self, str UPLO="L")`` defaults UPLO, so it 

166 # has to default here too or ``torch.linalg.eigvalsh(A)`` fails to bind. 

167 logger.debug("GEMS_ENFLAME_GCU400 LINALG_EIGVALSH") 

168 if UPLO not in ("L", "U"): 

169 raise RuntimeError( 

170 "Expected UPLO argument to be 'L' or 'U', but got " + str(UPLO) 

171 ) 

172 if self.dim() < 2: 

173 raise RuntimeError( 

174 "linalg.eigh: The input tensor A must have at least 2 dimensions." 

175 ) 

176 if self.shape[-1] != self.shape[-2]: 

177 raise RuntimeError( 

178 "linalg.eigh: A must be batches of square matrices, but they are %d by %d matrices" 

179 % (self.shape[-2], self.shape[-1]) 

180 ) 

181 

182 n = int(self.shape[-1]) 

183 # An empty matrix has no eigenvalues; ATen returns the empty result rather 

184 # than dividing by the zero-sized matrix order. 

185 if n == 0 or self.numel() == 0: 

186 return torch.empty(self.shape[:-2] + (n,), device=self.device, dtype=self.dtype) 

187 

188 B = int(self.numel() // (n * n)) 

189 mat = self.reshape(B, n, n) 

190 

191 N = triton.next_power_of_2(max(n, 1)) 

192 out = torch.empty((B, n), device=self.device, dtype=self.dtype) 

193 

194 # Relative skip threshold for threshold-Jacobi. It is far below the 

195 # accuracy the declared output dtype can carry, so skipped rotations cannot 

196 # move an eigenvalue beyond the tolerance. 

197 if self.dtype == torch.float64: 

198 thresh = 1e-13 

199 elif self.dtype == torch.float32: 

200 thresh = 1e-7 

201 else: 

202 thresh = 1e-4 

203 

204 _eigvalsh_jacobi_kernel[(B,)]( 

205 mat, 

206 out, 

207 mat.stride(0), 

208 mat.stride(1), 

209 mat.stride(2), 

210 out.stride(0), 

211 NP=n, 

212 N=N, 

213 SWEEPS=_SWEEPS, 

214 UPLO_L=(UPLO == "L"), 

215 THRESH=thresh, 

216 num_warps=1, 

217 ) 

218 return out.reshape(self.shape[:-2] + (n,)) 

219 

220 

221def linalg_eigvalsh_out(self, UPLO="L", *, out): 

222 """Out overload of ``linalg_eigvalsh``. 

223 

224 ``linalg_eigvalsh.out`` decomposes to ``_linalg_eigh`` rather than to the 

225 default overload, so without this entry an ``out=`` call never reaches the 

226 kernel above. Like ATen, a mismatched ``out`` dtype is rejected instead of 

227 being cast, and a wrongly-shaped ``out`` is resized. 

228 """ 

229 logger.debug("GEMS_ENFLAME_GCU400 LINALG_EIGVALSH_OUT") 

230 result = linalg_eigvalsh(self, UPLO) 

231 if out.dtype != result.dtype: 

232 raise RuntimeError( 

233 "Expected out tensor to have dtype %s, but got %s instead" 

234 % (result.dtype, out.dtype) 

235 ) 

236 out.resize_(result.shape) 

237 out.copy_(result) 

238 return out
